title: American Dollhouse horror trailer reveals January release
excerpt:
John Valley returns with a domestic horror feature.
Dark Star Films sets a January 15 U.S. release.
body_md:
Dark Star Films has unveiled the official trailer for American Dollhouse and announced a January 15, 2027 release in the United States. Directed by Austin-based filmmaker John Valley, the horror feature follows a woman whose attempt to rebuild her life turns into a dangerous encounter with an obsessively intrusive neighbor. The film was shot in Austin, Texas.

Hailley Laurén, whose previous credits include the television series 1923, leads the cast. Her character inherits her childhood home and decides to move back into the property in the hope of making a fresh start. What initially appears to be an opportunity to regain stability becomes increasingly threatening when she discovers that a disturbed neighbor is stalking her. The familiar associations of home and family gradually give way to an escalating nightmare.

Laurén is joined by Kelsey Pribilski, Tinus Seaux, Danielle Evon Ploeger and Richard C. Jones. Pribilski previously appeared in Man Finds Tape, while Seaux has a connection to Valley's earlier feature The Pizzagate Massacre. Ploeger's credits include RATS!, and Jones has appeared in the television miniseries Love & Death.

American Dollhouse marks Valley's second feature as a director. His 2020 debut, The Pizzagate Massacre, attracted attention among horror audiences and established his connection to independent genre filmmaking. His latest project has already had an opportunity to reach festival audiences ahead of its wider American release.

The film received its world premiere at SXSW in 2026 before appearing at additional genre festivals. These included France's L’Etrange Festival and the Brooklyn Horror Film Festival. Its festival journey provides context for the release announcement, although festival selection alone should not be treated as evidence of critical consensus or commercial success.

David Axe, Samuel Butler, Shane Greb, Christian Sosa and Jon Wroblewski produced the feature. Sosa and Wroblewski are associated with Roosevelt Film Lab.

From a thematic perspective, the premise draws on the unsettling transformation of a familiar domestic environment into a source of danger. A childhood home normally carries associations of memory, belonging and personal security. A story that places an obsessive threat within that environment can use the contrast between familiarity and vulnerability to generate psychological tension. Whether the finished film delivers on that potential remains a matter for audiences to discover.

The announced January release applies to the United States. The available announcement does not establish a digital release date, an international rollout or availability on any particular streaming service.
